title: How to Explain an Employment Gap in Your Cover Letter (One Honest Line)
summary: Should you mention an employment gap in your cover letter? How to handle it in one honest line, where to put it, what to say and omit, framed by gap type.
body_text: How do you explain an employment gap in a cover letter? If the gap is short or old, skip it. Your cover letter sells why you fit, not why you were away. When a gap is long, recent, or plainly visible on your resume, handle it in one calm sentence: the honest reason in plain terms, a note that you are ready to get back to it, and then straight back to the role. Put that line in the body or near the end, never the opening. No apology, no backstory, no fudged dates. One line, then move on. Here is the mistake almost everyone makes with a gap. They treat the cover letter like a courtroom where they have to defend the missing months before the recruiter will hear anything else. So the letter opens with the gap, spends a paragraph on it, apologizes twice, and buries the actual reason to hire them somewhere in the last line nobody reaches. A cover letter is a pitch, not a defense. The recruiter reading it has a stack of other applicants and roughly a coffee's worth of patience, and what they want to know first is can you do the job. The gap is a side note in that pitch, if it belongs there at all. Most of the time you can settle the whole question in a single sentence, and a lot of the time you should not raise it in the letter at all. This piece is about that one sentence. When to write it, where to put it, exactly what to say and what to leave out, and how to shape it for the specific reason you were away. If your bigger question is whether a gap even hurts your chances anymore, we answered that one separately in do employers actually care about career gaps . Here we are past that. You have decided the cover letter is the place to touch it, and you want to do it well. Should you even mention the gap at all? Start here, because the answer is often no, and a lot of people talk themselves into a problem they did not have. If nobody is going to raise an eyebrow at your timeline, do not draw a box around it and point. The test is not "do I have a gap." It is "does this gap create a question the reader will silently ask." Three things decide that. Size: a couple of months between jobs reads as normal life, not a red flag. Age: a gap from four years and two jobs ago has already been answered by everything you have done since. Visibility: if your resume is written in years and the gap barely shows, it may not register at all. Run your own timeline through that and most short or old gaps fall away. A recruiter who has screened a few hundred applications this year is not going to stop on three quiet months in 2023. Nurses, tradespeople, anyone in a field starved for staff, get even more slack. Point that same energy at a gap that is a year long, ended last month, or sits right at the top of your resume where the eye lands, and the calculus flips. That one the reader will notice regardless of what you write. Silence there does not make it invisible. It just leaves the reader to fill in the blank themselves, and people fill blanks with worst cases. So the honest rule is calibrated, not absolute. Small, old, or buried, leave it alone and spend the words on your fit. Big, recent, or obvious, a short preemptive line beats a loud silence. You are choosing between a question you control and a question you do not. The one-line principle When you do address it, the whole thing lives or dies on length. One sentence. Two if the second one is short and points forward. That is the ceiling, and treating it as the ceiling is what separates a confident applicant from a nervous one. The shape is simple. Name the reason in plain words. If it is true, add a half-clause that you are ready and glad to get back to the work. Then pivot hard into why this role. That pivot is the important part. The gap sentence should hand off momentum, not stall it. The whole move fits in a breath: you had a personal or family or health matter that needed handling, it has been handled, you are fully committed to your career, and if they want more they can ask in the interview. Do not go into detail. If they probe, steer back to your fit. That is all of it. Everything past that first sentence is you undoing the calm you just built. Brevity works because it sends a signal, not because it is polite. A short, level sentence tells the reader the gap is a settled fact you are not anxious about. A long one tells them the opposite, that this is a wound you are still pressing on, which invites them to press on it too. You are not hiding anything by keeping it to a line. You are demonstrating that there is nothing here worth a paragraph. What to actually say The words themselves should be neutral, true, and forward-facing. Neutral means no charged language, nothing that reads as bitter or wounded or defensive. True means you are not inventing a story you would have to keep straight later. Forward-facing means the sentence ends pointed at the job, not stuck in the past. A working template, and you can hear how little it commits to: after taking time away for a family matter, I am eager to return to X and bring Y to your team. Swap "family matter" for whatever is honest and the rest holds. Notice what it does. It states a reason without a diagnosis, signals readiness, and lands on the role. A recruiter reads that and moves on, which is exactly the outcome you want. If you kept a hand in during the time off, one clause about it earns its place. A course you finished, freelance or volunteer work in your field, a certification. That does double duty: it explains the time and shows your skills did not rust, which is the actual thing a careful reader worries about. Do not stretch this. A single genuine detail beats a padded list that smells like justification. What to leave out This list matters more than the one above, because the failures here are the ones that sink letters. No backstory. The reader does not need the sequence of events, the diagnosis, the family situation, the falling-out. "A health matter, now fully resolved" is a complete sentence about a health gap. Anything past "now resolved" is oversharing, and oversharing a medical or personal detail does not build sympathy, it builds discomfort and invites questions you would rather not field. No apology. You are not sorry for having a life. Groveling reads as weakness, and it plants the idea that the gap is something to be sorry about, which is the frame you are trying to avoid. Never the word "fired," never "let go" in bitter terms. Layoffs and separations are common and carry no stigma when stated plainly, but the second you editorialize you have made yourself the problem. Keep it factual. If you left under a cloud, the cover letter is the last place to relitigate it, and the interview is where a "why did you leave" answer belongs anyway, which we cover in explaining a career gap in the interview . And here is the one that ends job searches: do not lie, and do not fudge your dates. This feels like the safe move when you are panicking, so it is worth being clear about why it is the opposite. Employment dates are verifiable. Background screeners routinely confirm them through payroll databases like The Work Number, and the "I was freelancing" cover story now gets tested too, because a real business is registered and filed returns. When one date does not check out, it is not a small problem. It makes everything else you submitted suspect, and that is usually the end of the offer. We walk through exactly what a screen confirms in what a background check actually shows , and the whole case against fudging dates in the career-gaps piece . The short version: an honest gap costs you far less than a caught lie. Where the line goes in the letter Placement is half the battle. The single most common error, after over-explaining, is leading with the gap. Do not open on it. The first line of a cover letter has one job, which is to make the reader want to keep reading, and "I have been unemployed for the past year" does the reverse. You have spent your best real estate on your weakest fact. The opening belongs to fit and interest. Say who you are and why this role, in a way that makes the reader lean in. If you want to nail that first sentence, we have a whole guide on how to start a cover letter that does not waste it. The gap line goes later, once you have earned some goodwill. The body works well, tucked after you have established what you bring, framed as a quick bit of context on the way to your close. Near the end works too, folded into the "here is where I am now and why I am excited about this" beat. By then the reader already sees a capable candidate, so the gap arrives as a footnote to a strong pitch instead of the headline. Same sentence, completely different weight, depending only on where you set it down. Not sure where the gap line should sit in your letter? Build a tailored cover letter with the fit up front and the gap handled in one clean sentence, using guided prompts and ready-made structure. Write your cover letter → Framing the line by gap type The one-line principle holds across every reason, but the exact wording shifts. Here is how to land each of the common ones. Each is a neutral reason plus a forward turn, and each is short on purpose. Layoff or restructuring This is the easy one, because it carries no stigma anymore. Whole teams get cut for reasons that have nothing to do with the people in them, and every recruiter knows it. State it flat: my role was eliminated in a restructuring, and I have been focused on finding the right next fit rather than the fastest one. Done. One caveat worth knowing: if you are still employed and just looking, you do not have a gap yet, so there is nothing to mention. Do not manufacture one. A short example line: "Following a company-wide restructuring earlier this year, I have been selective about my next move, and this role is exactly the kind of work I want to get back to." Caregiving or parental leave Matter-of-fact is the register here. You took time to care for family, and now you are ready to return. No detailed accounting of who needed what. "I stepped away to care for a family member and am now fully available and eager to get back to work in X" says everything a reader needs. Parental leave is even simpler and even more normal. The old instinct to hide a stint at home has aged badly, and the honest one-liner reads as competent, not apologetic. Health Minimal, minimal, minimal. A health gap gets the fewest words of any category, because detail here is all downside. "A health matter that is now fully resolved" is the whole sentence. Do not name the condition, do not narrate the recovery, do not reassure at length that it will not recur, because reassurance at length does the opposite of reassure. The word "resolved" carries the load. Then pivot to the role and let the resolved gap sit quietly behind your fit. Education or reskilling This is the one gap you can frame as a plus, so frame it as a plus. Name the credential. "I spent the past year completing a data analytics certificate to move deeper into X" is not an excuse, it is an investment the reader can see paying off in the job you are applying for. If you retooled specifically toward this field, say so plainly. A reskilling gap is often the best possible use of time off, and the letter should sound like you know that. Sabbatical, travel, or relocation Brief and confident is the whole play. You do not owe anyone an apology for a planned break or a move, so do not sound like you are seeking permission. "After a planned break to travel, I am back and focused on the next chapter of my work in X" is plenty. Relocation is even more mundane: you moved, you are settled, you are looking. State it and move on. Confidence is the tell here. A sabbatical stated apologetically reads as a cover story; the same sabbatical stated plainly reads as exactly what it was. Remember the gap is a footnote, not the subject Zoom out for a second, because it is easy to lose this while you are agonizing over the phrasing. In a good cover letter the gap should be maybe five percent of the words and none of the emphasis. If you read your draft back and the missing months are the thing that stands out, you have written the wrong letter. Everything around that one line should be about the work. Why you want this role, what you bring, what you have done that maps to what they need. The gap sentence is a speed bump the reader clears on the way to the good stuff, not a wall you make them climb. A useful gut check: cover the gap line with your thumb and read the rest. If what remains is a strong, specific pitch, you are fine, and the gap line just adds a bit of context. If what remains is thin, the problem was never the gap. It was that the letter was not selling you hard enough. Does a recruiter even read the cover letter? Fair question, and the honest answer is: sometimes, and less often than you would hope. Plenty of recruiters skip cover letters entirely, especially on high-volume roles where they are triaging hundreds of applications and reading a written statement from each one is not physically possible. If you want the full picture of where the cover letter sits in the process, our walkthrough of how hiring actually works maps every stage from apply to offer. But here is the part that matters for you. The recruiters who do open a cover letter often do it precisely to answer a question the resume raised, and a visible gap is one of the top questions on that list. So the calculus is not "will they read it," it is "if they read it, what will they find." A clean one-line explanation waiting there is a small, cheap insurance policy against the version where they wonder and guess. And if the gap is the main thing your letter adds that your resume cannot, that is a legitimate reason to bother writing one at all, which we cover in when a cover letter actually wins . Write it short, write it human, and let it do that one job well. Tone: write it like a person, not a legal filing The gap line fails more often on tone than on content. Stiff, formal, defensive phrasing is what makes a perfectly fine explanation sound like an admission. Read your sentence out loud. If it sounds like something you would say to a colleague you respect, keep it. If it sounds like a disclosure statement, rewrite it warmer and shorter. This is really just the whole cover letter working the way it should. The best ones read like a short, direct note to a real human being, which is the case we make in writing a cover letter like an email . A gap handled in that voice barely registers as a problem. The same fact wrapped in corporate throat-clearing reads as a problem the writer is nervous about, and nervous is contagious. Level and human beats formal and apologetic every time. Fit it into your existing template You do not need a special cover letter for a gap. You need your normal one with a single sentence added in the right place. If you already work from a reusable structure, and you should, the gap line drops cleanly into the body paragraph without disturbing the rest of it. Our reusable cover letter template is built so you can keep most of it fixed and swap only the parts that change per application. The gap sentence is one of those swappable parts. Keep it in a note somewhere, tuned to your situation, and paste it into the body when the role warrants it. That way you are not rewriting the hard part every time, and you are not tempted to over-explain because you are typing it fresh under pressure. If you would rather work from guided structure than a blank page, Hiration's cover letter builder keeps the fit up front and gives you a clean spot to drop the gap line without letting it take over. The whole gap treatment fits inside the workflow you already have. It is one line, in one paragraph, in the letter you were going to write anyway. The bigger picture in 2026 Gaps are not what they were. Between mass layoffs, the caregiving crunch, and everything the last few years did to normal career timelines, a clean unbroken run is no longer the default a hiring manager expects to see. Recruiters know searches take longer now. Many will tell you outright that a gap under a couple of years does not register as an issue when the experience lines up, and that the only gap that actually worries them is the unexplained one paired with stale skills. That reframes the whole exercise. Rather than damage control, the one honest line is you closing an open loop before the reader has to, so the conversation can move to the thing that matters, which is what you can actually do for them. Handle the resume side of a return with the same calm, using something like our guide to a career gap resume , keep your skills current so there is a real answer behind the sentence, and the gap stops being a liability and becomes a footnote you controlled. The letter's job was never to grovel. It was to sell you and, in one level line, close the one question standing between the reader and your fit. Frequently Asked Questions Do I have to mention my employment gap in the cover letter? No, and often you should not. If the gap is short, old, or barely visible on your resume, leave it out and spend the words on why you fit. Address it only when it is long, recent, or sits somewhere the reader will clearly notice. Then one line does it. How do I word a gap in one sentence? Neutral reason, forward turn, back to the job. Something like: "After taking time away for a family matter, I am eager to return to X and bring Y to your team." State the reason plainly, signal you are ready, then pivot straight into the role. No detail, no apology. If you want full letters to model the flow, our cover letter examples show the structure in context. Where in the cover letter should the gap line go? Not the opening. Lead with fit and interest so the reader wants to keep going. Slot the gap sentence into the body or near the end, after you have established what you bring. By then it reads as a footnote to a strong pitch instead of the headline. Should I explain a layoff in my cover letter? Only briefly, and only if it left a visible gap. Layoffs carry no stigma now, so state it flat: your role was eliminated in a restructuring and you are focused on the right next fit. If you are still employed and just looking, there is no gap yet, so do not mention it at all. How much detail should I give about a health gap? As little as possible. "A health matter that is now fully resolved" is the entire sentence. Do not name the condition or narrate the recovery. The word "resolved" carries the weight, and extra reassurance reads as anxiety rather than confidence. Is it okay to say I was caregiving? Yes, and keep it matter-of-fact. "I stepped away to care for a family member and am now fully available to get back to work in X" covers it without an accounting of who needed what. Caregiving and parental leave are common and read as competent when stated plainly. Can I just fudge my dates to hide the gap? No. Employment dates get verified through payroll databases and reference checks, and a "freelancing" cover story gets tested too. One date that does not check out makes everything else on your application suspect and usually ends the offer. An honest gap costs far less than a caught lie. Should I apologize for the gap? Never. You are not sorry for having a life, and apologizing plants the idea that the gap is something to be sorry about. Keep the sentence level and confident. The tone you use tells the reader more than the words do, and calm reads as capable. What if the recruiter never reads the cover letter? Some will not, especially on high-volume roles. But the ones who do open it often do so to answer a question the resume raised, and a visible gap is near the top of that list. A ready one-line explanation is cheap insurance against the reader wondering and guessing. Does a gap actually hurt my chances in 2026? Usually less than you fear. Recruiters know searches run long now, and most weigh trajectory and fit over a gap. The real risk is an unexplained gap paired with stale skills. We cover whether gaps hurt in depth in our piece on whether employers care about career gaps . title: Duke Energy awards more than $50,000 in emergency grants to support Indiana storm recovery
summary: Duke Energy and its foundation are reaching out to its communities affected by last week’s historic floods with more than $50,000 in emergency grants.
body_text: Funding will help local organizations provide food assistance, cleanup support, other resources to communities impacted by severe weather, flooding PLAINFIELD, Ind. – Duke Energy and its foundation are reaching out to its communities affected by last week’s historic floods with more than $50,000 in emergency grants. “Our line crews and support teams who worked to restore power saw firsthand the devastating impacts of last week’s storms and historic flooding on the Indiana cities and towns we serve,” said Duke Energy Indiana President Stan Pinegar. “We know the rebuilding process is just beginning and communities have immediate needs.” The rapid response grants will support food assistance, storm cleanup and other immediate recovery needs. Grant recipients include: Wayne County Community Foundation – $10,000 toward clean-up, restoration and social services in Cambridge City and Milton Franklin County Community Foundation – $10,000 to support flood recovery community needs Fayette County Community Foundation – $10,000 to support Connersville and Fayette County flood recovery Hamilton County Community Foundation – $7,500 to support restoration of damages in parks in the county Food Finders Food Bank – $5,000 to help replenish food supplies and support residents in Camden Henry County Community Foundation – $5,000 to support flood recovery community needs Sycamore Land Trust – $2,500 to support storm cleanup and trail restoration in Bloomington Brazil City Fire Department – $2,500 to support city’s response to natural disasters, including equipment purchases “Flooding can be incredibly disruptive and create lasting challenges for communities long after flood waters recede,” said Loree Elswick, president of the Duke Energy Foundation. “These grants will help local organizations provide assistance, support recovery efforts and address needs in our communities.” Duke Energy Foundation The Duke Energy Foundation provides nearly $30 million annually in philanthropic support to meet the needs of communities where Duke Energy customers live and work. The Foundation is funded by Duke Energy shareholders. Duke Energy Indiana Duke Energy Indiana, a subsidiary of Duke Energy, provides about 6,800 megawatts of owned electric capacity to approximately 930,000 customers in a 23,000-square-mile service area, making it Indiana’s largest electric supplier. Contact: Angeline Protogere Phone: 800.559.3853 X: @DukeEnergyIN

title: Globalstar Confirms Successful Launch of All 8 HIBLEO-4 Replacement Satellites
summary: Satellites launched aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket reach orbital plane COVINGTON, La., Aug. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Globalstar (NASDAQ: GSAT), a next-generation telecommunications infrastructure and technology provider, today announced the successful launch and deployment of its latest
body_text: Globalstar Confirms Successful Launch of All 8 HIBLEO-4 Replacement Satellites August 16, 2026 at 9:20 AM EDT Satellites launched aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket reach orbital plane COVINGTON, La., Aug. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Globalstar (NASDAQ: GSAT), a next-generation telecommunications infrastructure and technology provider, today announced the successful launch and deployment of its latest satellites, marking another significant milestone in the continued expansion of the Company's low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation. Following a successful launch, all satellites were successfully dispensed from the launch vehicle and have reached their intended orbital planes. Globalstar's Satellite Operations Command Center team has established communications with each satellite, and all are currently under the Company's command and control. Initial health assessments indicate the satellites are performing as expected, and engineers are actively monitoring their status as they progress through early orbit operations. "The successful launch and deployment of these satellites is an important milestone for Globalstar and our customers around the world," said Dr. Paul E. Jacobs, Globalstar CEO. "With all satellites safely in their intended orbital planes and under our command and control, we are pleased with the mission's progress and are now focused on completing early orbit operations for the satellites to provide additional resiliency across our network." The newly launched satellites will undergo a series of commissioning activities, including comprehensive system testing and calibration, before being integrated into Globalstar's operational constellation. These activities are designed to verify satellite performance and ensure they meet the Company's rigorous operational standards prior to entering commercial service. Additional updates on the commissioning process and the satellites' entry into operational service will be provided as key milestones are achieved. About Globalstar, Inc. Globalstar is a global telecommunications provider connecting what matters most. Through our industry-leading low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation and licensed Band 53/n53 spectrum, we deliver reliable satellite and terrestrial connectivity solutions that empower customers worldwide to connect, transmit, and communicate smarter. Our comprehensive connectivity ecosystem includes software-defined, purpose-built private wireless network platform, coupled with Globalstar Band 53 in XCOM RAN™ and trusted GPS messengers Saved by SPOT™ for safety and personal communication for business and enterprise applications. Serving business, enterprise, and consumer markets across the globe, Globalstar supports applications that track and protect assets, enable automation, enhance operational efficiency, and safeguard lives. With unmatched reach and a relentless focus on innovation, and mission-critical performance, we're redefining what's possible for global connectivity. To learn more, visit www.globalstar.com . Media Contact: Alisa Moloney Alisa.Moloney@globalstar.com A photo accompanying this announcement is available at: https://www.globenewswire.com/NewsRoom/AttachmentNg/3b30ddab-95b1-450c-9b66-e035aac38b6c Globalstar HIBLEO-4 Launch Globalstar confirms the successful launch of all 8 HIBLEO-4 replacement satellites aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket.

body_text: Palladyne AI (PDYN) reported a sharp acceleration in second-quarter revenue as its defense, aerospace and autonomous-systems businesses begin converting contract activity into sales. Q2 2026 by the Numbers: Palladyne AI — Q2 2026 Result Change / Context Revenue $5.8M +470% YoY Sequential Revenue Growth — +63% QoQ Backlog $24.6M +43% QoQ New Q2 Contract Awards ~$13.0M New awards during quarter Cash + Marketable Securities $43.7M Roughly flat QoQ Operating Loss ($13.4M) vs. ($8.1M) prior year GAAP Net Loss ($12.3M) — GAAP EPS ($0.27) — FY2026 Revenue Guidance $24M–$27M +357% to +415% YoY FY2026 Operating Cash Burn Guidance $32M–$36M ~$8M–$9M/quarter average Palladyne added approximately $13 million of new contract awards during Q2, allowing backlog to grow 43% even after recognizing a record quarter of revenue. Management expects the majority of that backlog to convert to revenue over the next 12–18 months. Palladyne reiterated full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $24M–$27M That would represent approximately 357%–415% year-over-year growth from $5.2 million in 2025. Management also expects revenue to increase sequentially again in Q3 as backlog converts and new programs ramp. The company maintained expected 2026 operating cash burn of $32M–$36M, or an average of approximately $8M–$9M per quarter. Management expects cash usage to decline through the remainder of the year as revenue and margins increase. Defense Programs Are Becoming More Concrete The quarter included several notable program milestones: $2.6M of BRAIN flight-computer orders, including a $2.3M contract supporting a low-cost kinetic counter-UAS interceptor. A $2.9M U.S. Air Force STRATFI option , bringing the total Palladyne IQ program value above $10.6M . Commencement of a previously announced $4.2M Air Force Research Laboratory HANGTIME contract . Competitive selection for two U.S. Army contracts to operationally validate SwarmOS and Gremlin-X. Five additional defense exercises scheduled through March 2027 following recent SwarmOS demonstrations. Palladyne also signed an exclusive partnership with Israel Aerospace Industries covering U.S. rights to HARPY, HAROP and Mini HARPY long-range loitering munitions, with up to 10 years of exclusivity. One Operator. Four Drone Manufacturers The SwarmOS demonstration may be particularly important to the longer-term robotics story. During the Army's Ivy Mass exercise, Palladyne integrated SwarmOS into the Army's next-generation command-and-control ecosystem. The system enabled one operator to control drones from four different manufacturers, including Palladyne's Gremlin-X. Palladyne remains an early-stage company, and losses and cash consumption remain significant. $1.0M → $5.8M quarterly revenue $17.3M → $24.6M backlog in one quarter ~$13M of new Q2 awards $24M–$27M FY26 revenue guidance PDYN's Commercialization Dashboard Q2 Revenue Growth +470% Sequential Growth +63% Backlog Growth +43% QoQ Q2 New Awards ~$13M Backlog $24.6M FY26 Revenue Target $24M–$27M Implied FY Growth +357% to +415% $24.6M of backlog versus $5.8M of quarterly revenue . Backlog is about 4.3× Q2 revenue , and Palladyne expects most of it to convert over 12–18 months.

title: Finding a Decedent's PBGC Pension During Probate (August 2026)
summary: This August 2026 guide explains how to search PBGC for a decedent's pension benefits, report a death, and claim survivor benefits as an executor.
body_text: When a private-sector employer shuts down or goes bankrupt, the pension plans it sponsored don't simply disappear. A federal agency called the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (PBGC) steps in, takes over those plans, and holds the money until participants or their families come forward to claim it. For estate settlement, if a decedent held a private-sector job during their career, a PBGC search is worth running. The search is free, and requires only the decedent's last name and the last four digits of their Social Security number. Key Takeaways You can search pbgc.gov for free using the decedent's last name and last four SSN digits. Roughly 80,000 workers had unclaimed PBGC benefits as of 2026. A will does not control PBGC beneficiary designations; whoever is named on file with PBGC receives the benefit. Elayne's Verified Asset Search covers PBGC and 100+ financial sources as part of a single benefit discovery process. What the PBGC Is and What Plans It Covers The Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation is a federal agency that insures private-sector defined benefit pension plans. When a covered plan terminates without enough money to pay promised benefits, the PBGC steps in and takes over payment responsibility directly. These are traditional pension plans that promise a specific monthly payment at retirement, calculated from factors like years of service and salary history. They are distinct from 401(k)s and defined contribution plans , which PBGC does not insure. PBGC coverage is also limited to private-sector employers. Several common plan types fall entirely outside its scope: Federal government pensions (Civil Service, FERS, CSRS) Military retirement benefits State and local government pensions Church plans Most plans covering only business owners or partners {{blog-cta-financial}} How to Search the PBGC Unclaimed Benefits Database The PBGC maintains a free searchable database. It can be used by those with permission to access the decedent's identifying information. To run a search, you need two pieces of information: The decedent's last name The last four digits of their Social Security number How to Run the Search The unclaimed pension search tool is available at pbgc.gov. The search field accepts the decedent's last name as it would appear on employment records, along with the last four digits of their Social Security number. Any matching records across PBGC's database of participants in terminated or trusteed plans are returned. A few aspects of the search to note: The database updates quarterly, so a plan that terminated recently may not yet appear in results The search is exact-match on name, meaning a maiden name or hyphenated surname used at any point in the decedent's career would require a separate search for each variation Only the last four SSN digits are required, which helps limit exposure of sensitive information during the search What a Result Actually Means A positive result means the PBGC has a record of a benefit associated with that individual and has not yet made contact or confirmed payment. The next steps involve contacting PBGC directly to identify the plan, confirm the decedent's identity, and determine whether a survivor benefit applies. A negative result could mean: no covered plan exists for that individual, the benefit was already claimed, or that the plan has not yet been processed into the database. The PBGC Missing Participants Program Explained When a retirement plan terminates, administrators must account for every participant, including those they cannot locate. For PBGC-insured single-employer and multiemployer defined benefit plans, transferring missing participants to the Missing Participants Program is mandatory. Defined contribution plans like 401(k)s can participate voluntarily if they terminated on or after January 1, 2018, when the program expanded beyond traditional pensions. Funds transferred through the program are not frozen. They grow at the federal mid-term rate while held, so a benefit that sat unclaimed for years may be worth more than the original plan statement indicated. The PBGC Trusteed Plans Search and Insured Plans Search The PBGC unclaimed benefits database is not the only place to search. PBGC maintains two additional searchable directories that executors can check. The Trusteed Plans search lists every plan PBGC has taken over as trustee following a distress or involuntary termination. If the decedent's former employer went through bankruptcy or shut down with an underfunded plan, PBGC likely became trustee and now pays benefits directly. You can search this directory by employer name. A match confirms PBGC controls the plan and is the right contact for any survivor benefit claim. The Insured Plans search covers plans that are still ongoing but insured by PBGC. If a plan appears here, it has not yet terminated, meaning the plan administrator handles benefit payments and participant records, not PBGC. In that case, you can contact the plan administrator directly using the employer information listed. Search What It Covers How to Search Who Handles Payments Unclaimed Benefits Benefits PBGC holds for participants it has not yet contacted or confirmed payment for Last name + last 4 SSN digits at pbgc.gov PBGC Trusteed Plans Plans PBGC took over as trustee after a distress or involuntary termination (e.g., employer bankruptcy) Employer name at pbgc.gov PBGC Insured Plans Active plans still insured by PBGC that have not yet terminated Employer name at pbgc.gov Plan administrator What to Do When the Decedent Appears in the Database To move forward, you can call PBGC directly at 1-800-400-7242 and identify yourself as the executor or personal representative of the decedent's estate. Having the following ready before the call is helpful: The decedent's full legal name and Social Security number A copy of the death certificate Your Letters Testamentary or other court-issued authority document Your own government-issued ID PBGC will use these to verify the decedent's identity and confirm your legal authority to act on behalf of the estate. Without documented authority, PBGC cannot release account or plan information to you, regardless of your relationship to the decedent. After the call, PBGC typically mails correspondence to the executor's location of record. Response times vary, but follow-up letters generally arrive within a few weeks. If you do not hear back, you can call again with your case reference number. Once identity and authority are confirmed, PBGC can help clarify the benefit amount, any applicable survivor benefit options, and what forms are needed to start payment. {{blog-cta-financial}} How Executors Report a Death and Claim Survivor Benefits When a PBGC-covered participant dies, two separate questions arise: whether the estate is owed any unpaid benefit payments, and whether a survivor benefit is payable to a named beneficiary. The answer to both depends on the annuity form the decedent elected when benefits began. PBGC will request the death certificate, Letters Testamentary or a court appointment order, and the participant's Social Security number. Once submitted, PBGC reviews the participant's file to confirm the elected annuity option. There are two common outcomes depending on what the decedent chose: A single-life annuity ends at death with no survivor benefit payable to the estate or any beneficiary. A joint-and-survivor annuity continues payments to the named surviving beneficiary after the participant's death. Any payments issued after the date of death but before PBGC was notified may need to be returned. How Elayne Supports Pension and Benefit Discovery During Estate Settlement Elayne's Verified Asset Search reaches across 100+ financial sources, covering unclaimed property databases and PBGC as part of a single credentialed discovery process. Survivor benefits, including Social Security, pension, and veterans' benefits, are surfaced through a structured identification step so the executor does not need to locate them independently. A shared dashboard keeps co-executors, attorneys, and family members aligned on what has been confirmed and what still needs follow-up. For estates that include inherited retirement accounts, Elayne also tracks inherited IRA distribution rules and SECURE Act 2.0 distribution deadlines and mandatory annual RMD requirements. FAQ How do I search the PBGC unclaimed pensions database for a decedent's benefits as an executor? The PBGC unclaimed pensions database accepts the decedent's last name and the last four digits of their Social Security number. Because the search is exact-match on name, maiden names or hyphenated surnames used at any point in the decedent's career each require a separate search, since name variations will return different results. What is the National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits? The National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits is a free, voluntary registry where employers register former employees who left without claiming 401(k) or pension benefits. How to find a deceased parent's unclaimed pension and retirement benefits in 2026? The PBGC unclaimed pensions database is a helpful resource for defined benefit pensions, as are the National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits and every state unclaimed property database. What happens to a PBGC pension benefit if the decedent elected a single-life annuity? A single-life annuity ends at the participant's death with no survivor benefit payable to the estate or any named beneficiary. Only a joint-and-survivor annuity continues payments after death, and those payments go to whoever is on file with PBGC, not to whoever is named in the will, since PBGC beneficiary designations are governed entirely by plan records and are not controlled by a court-admitted will. *Disclaimer: This article is for informational purposes only and does not provide legal, medical, financial, or tax advice. Please consult with a licensed professional to address your specific situation.

title: Building a Context Layer for AI Agents | Snowflake
summary: Learn best practices for creating a semantic layer using Snowflake semantic views. Improve data accuracy and scale AI agent performance across your stack.
body_text: Modern enterprises collect and manage millions of data sources and signals across their business. At Snowflake, we use Snowflake internally to monitor our business systems and product telemetry at scale — across every query, warehouse and click. But without a shared understanding, petabytes of raw data become a source of conflicting answers, not a foundation for action. To leverage our data at scale for both humans and AI agents, we curate an internal semantic layer. This post covers how we built our context layer using semantics and the best practices we learned in the process. Figure 1: Snowflake’s internal environment uses a semantic layer to empower every entity to query consistent and accurate data. The bottleneck was never the data — it was context The immense amount of internal telemetry makes it incredibly powerful, but that same scale makes failure modes frustrating. Take a seemingly simple question such as “What is an active customer?” That question could yield different answers across different tables and varying metric definitions: Active is WHERE days_since_last_login < 30 from the table login_counts Active is WHERE credits_consumed > 0 and account_type != ‘TRIAL’ from the table customers Active is COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) without a region identifier from the table customers_with_accounts Typically, based on our internal use cases and what we have seen from our customers, the burden of clarifying data’s meaning falls on data science teams: Humans design queries and confirm these queries with a trusted data scientist, who calls out flaws and gotchas. The alignment problem becomes exponentially worse with AI. New metrics and data sources are built at lightning speed, creating information gaps for even skilled analysts. If a Cortex Agent reports one number while a legacy dashboard shows another, no one knows which source to trust. One definition for every AI and BI interface Every interface needs consistent meaning, or context, for its data, which can be achieved by using a semantic layer. A semantic view is a top-level object that sits between the downstream consumers and raw data tables, translating governed business language into physical database schemas. Instead of exposing raw tables to dashboards or AI agents directly, the semantic view standardizes the data flow from physical tables to facts, dimensions and metrics. This gives people and tools consistent context about what the data means before they query it. Figure 2: Semantic views consist of logical names, metrics and AI metadata on top of physical tables to power downstream consumption. AI agents gain two benefits when using semantic views to query data at scale: Faster execution: Agents querying raw data spend time finding, understanding and sampling multiple data sources. At scale, these processes can dominate runtime. Instead, agents can use semantic views to go directly to SQL execution. Lower cost: Agents are significantly more token-efficient when using table relationships and join data in semantic views. With materialization, semantic SQL natively leverages preaggregated data, reducing repeated computation. With a semantic-oriented data architecture, returns compound quickly across the stack: Increased accuracy: Provide precise business context to models. In AtScale’s benchmark testing , adding semantic context increased text-to-SQL accuracy from 20% to more than 90% across 40 business questions on TPC-DS. One source of truth: Replace isolated, tool-specific semantics with a single semantic layer. Free governance: Leverage Snowflake’s access controls on semantic views and metric objects natively. True self-service: Support ad hoc, natural-language questions for any user on their own. "With semantic views we get a golden layer, a single trusted API for our data. With semantic view materializations, this one semantic API now works for every downstream consumer of our data, including use cases where query performance is critical. Now queries from dashboards, AI and ad hoc workflows can run through the same trusted data API." Zachary Blackwood Staff Data Scientist at Snowflake Snowflake’s internal product data science team uses an agent that leverages the internal semantic layer to field product questions from across the company. In July 2025 alone, more than 400 distinct internal users ran over 5,400 queries through the product data science agent and the semantic layer. And in the same time frame, more than 5,600 internal employees across all Snowflake teams and agents ran over 320,000 queries using the broad semantic layer in sales, HR, support and other areas. Figure 3: With a unified semantic layer, all tools and interfaces get one consistent, governed meaning of data. Best practices for the semantic layer Version, test and evaluate semantic views The semantic layer needs to be treated with the same rigor as production software. With Snowflake’s native data build tool (dbt) integration, we’re able to fully version control, peer review and apply continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) to our metrics. Though at Snowflake we primarily build semantic views using code, we use the UI to test and suggest improvements that integrate with our code. And because the UI and underlying code are perfectly synced, users can move between constructing a view in the Snowflake UI and committing fields to repositories easily. To evaluate semantic views, we needed access to the questions that people actually ask. A high-signal source for evals is popular dashboard tiles, which are constructed and used precisely to answer questions. We also log common questions to refine our eval sets. Prioritize performance with data engineering If your semantic layer sits on top of slow queries and poorly constructed tables, your AI agents will be slow. Early on, we tried pointing a semantic view at multiple raw, billion-count event tables. Every time a user asked a question, the view crawled and joined these tables, resulting in massive latency. Initially, we built and maintained our own preaggregated slices with Dynamic Tables. Each dashboard had the rollup and grain that it needed. However, as we expanded our semantic coverage to support new questions and domains, we had to manually add new pipelines and tables and maintain a rapidly growing estate. With semantic view materializations , we’re able to model semantic views directly on high-grain source tables and declare which dimension and metric combinations need to be fast. Snowflake intelligently maintains those slices for us in the background, helping reduce response times. As a bonus, we used Snowflake CoCo to draft and refine our semantic and data processes, as its built-in semantic view skills are purpose built for these use cases. Curate relentlessly and route intelligently A cluttered and inconsistent semantic layer defeats the purpose of standardizing metrics. For the key product areas that are frequently queried, we curate semantic views (using CoCo) to answer specific questions we have in mind. Every query is logged within Snowflake, including the returned results. With this, we’re able to easily build new semantic views and verified queries to continually expand our scope to what our users are asking. For intelligent routing, Cortex Agents automatically scan across all semantic views using our custom routing instructions to find the right context for a given query. And for broad coverage of the long tail of data, we lean on Cortex Sense, which evaluates data across our estate to help route questions to relevant data sets. Build your semantic layer today Raw data doesn't answer questions; context does. The semantic layer acts as this "golden layer" — defining business logic once to power every dashboard, Streamlit app and Cortex Agent across the agentic enterprise. We can get started with a useful semantic view in just one file. Note that we are using YAML in this example, but the use of SQL to define semantic views is also fully supported. name: account_activity_model tables: - name: daily_account_usage base_table: database: core schema: metrics table: daily_account_usage dimensions: - name: region expr: region data_type: VARCHAR description: "The geographic region of the account." # AI metadata synonyms: ["location", "geography", "area"] # AI metadata metrics: - name: compute_spend expr: SUM(credits_used) description: "The total number of Snowflake credits consumed." # AI metadata synonyms: ["cost", "spend", "credits used", "usage"] # AI metadata verified_queries: # AI metadata - name: total_spend question: "What is the total compute spend?" use_as_onboarding_question: true sql: | SELECT SUM(credits_used) AS compute_spend FROM core.metrics.daily_account_usage ORDER BY compute_spend DESC Now we can query the semantic view directly using standard SQL, without ever having to worry about underlying joins or raw column names: SELECT region, AGG(compute_spend) as compute_spend FROM account_activity_model GROUP BY region ORDER BY compute_spend DESC; For improved performance, we can also materialize this semantic view to preaggregate metrics (compute_spend) across dimensions (region): ALTER SEMANTIC VIEW account_activity_model SET MAX_STALENESS = '1 hour'; ALTER SEMANTIC VIEW account_activity_model ADD MATERIALIZATION spend_by_region WAREHOUSE = semantic_wh AS DIMENSIONS region METRICS compute_spend; Snowflake semantic views are also interoperable with Apache Ossie™ (incubating) . Ossie is the vendor-neutral, open standard for semantic and business context models. This allows you to use your semantics with the tool and platform of your choice. Even if your semantic models are stored elsewhere, you can always read them in Snowflake with a single function call: SELECT SYSTEM$READ_OSSIE_YAML_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW('db.schema.account_activity'); Semantics are the shared foundation for the entire AI and analytics stack. Get started with building a single, governed source of truth using Snowflake today, and stay tuned for a follow-up post where we’ll cover real-world customer case studies leveraging semantics in production.

body_text: Acquisition extends Versant’s leadership in golf and platforms, adding interactive sports capabilities across immersive play, training, entertainment and performance data NEW YORK--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Aug. 3, 2026-- Versant Media Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: VSNT) today announced the completion of its acquisition of Full Swing, a leading sports technology company whose patented hardware and integrated software are used by consumers, coaches, competitive athletes, and commercial venues. The acquisition extends Versant’s leadership in golf and deepens its portfolio of digital platforms. A trusted partner to many of the game’s top players, Full Swing serves one of the fastest-growing segments of the golf industry through immersive simulation, launch monitors, virtual greens, integrated software and performance data. Versant’s strength in golf uniquely positions the company to accelerate adoption of Full Swing’s technology across both consumer and commercial markets. Full Swing broadens Versant’s leadership within the golf ecosystem. Together with Golf Channel, GolfNow and GolfPass, Versant connects premium content, commerce, technology and participation, creating more ways to engage golfers throughout their journey. The platform also creates opportunities beyond golf, including baseball, where Full Swing’s technology is already used by both college and professional teams. With the transaction complete, Full Swing will operate within Versant’s Digital Platforms and Ventures portfolio and will be anchored in Versant’s golf business, supported by Golf Channel, GolfNow and GolfPass. Ryan Dotters, Chief Executive Officer of Full Swing, has joined Versant, reporting to Will McIntosh, President, Digital Platforms and Ventures. About Versant Media Group, Inc. Versant Media Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: VSNT) is an industry-changing media and entertainment business and home to trusted brands that shape culture, inform audiences, and build lasting connections. It operates in four core markets: political news and opinion; business news and personal finance; golf; and sports and genre entertainment. These markets are served through a powerful portfolio of iconic and innovative brands, including MS NOW, CNBC, USA Network, Golf Channel, E!, SYFY and Oxygen, and complementary digital platforms Fandango, Rotten Tomatoes, GolfNow and GolfPass. Visit www.versantmedia.com for more information. About Full Swing Full Swing is the industry leader in pioneering sports technology. Its lineup of trailblazing golf and baseball products entertains users around the world while helping them to practice with purpose. As the Official Licensed Simulator of the PGA TOUR and an Official Technology Partner of TGL presented by SoFi, Full Swing simulators bring unmatched real-ball-flight data to golf and immersive multi-sport experiences. The company’s KIT Launch Monitor, tested and trusted by Tiger Woods, is an indoor and outdoor practice solution that uniquely combines 16 points of club and ball data with high-resolution video. This groundbreaking technology has now been extended to baseball, so KIT can calculate both pre- and post-impact data performance insights like Squared Up Rate and Potential Exit Velocity. Full Swing’s impressive roster of champions is highlighted by PGA TOUR stars like Tiger Woods, Jordan Spieth, Jon Rahm, Xander Schauffele, and Dustin Johnson, as well as Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen and Steph Curry. title: The Mobile Deposits Dilemma
summary: How simulating MRDC risk rules helped banks boost mobile deposit adoption without increasing fraud losses.
body_text: With over 5,000 banks across the U.S., paper checks remain the default way to pay someone directly from a bank account. Processing them is costly, so banks have long sought alternatives to in-person teller deposits. The "Check 21" legislation of 2004 made a check image a legal substitute for the physical document. ATMs soon followed, introducing image processing technology capable of identifying the issuing bank and reading handwritten dollar amounts. Then, in 2009, USAA took the next leap: leveraging the growing popularity of mobile banking, it launched mobile remote deposit capture (MRDC)—a smartphone app that lets customers photograph the front and back of an endorsed check and submit it electronically.¹ MRDC was an early form of intelligent document processing, using AI to correct for creases and folds in the paper before parsing the handwritten amount. ¹ Becky Yerak, "New Wave of Banking: Check Deposit via Smart-phone Photo," July 2010. MRDC adoption: Benefits and risks During my banking career, I was asked to evaluate the costs and benefits of MRDC. My team carefully modeled the economic value of customer adoption and found the gains extended well beyond direct teller cost savings—MRDC also improved customer retention and drove higher deposit account balances. ² We further found that a customer's likelihood of adopting MRDC was closely tied to whether they were already moving money through the digital banking app. ² Gary Class, " Customer Banking Relationship in 5 Dimensions, " Teradata.com, 3 July 2024. That said, MRDC introduces real fraud risk: a deposited check could be counterfeit or drawn on an account with insufficient funds. To manage this exposure, banks imposed two safeguards—a per-item dollar limit and a daily aggregate cap on remotely deposited checks. These risk controls, however, made banks reluctant to promote MRDC broadly. Considering adoption as a control limits problem When I turned to identifying what was holding MRDC adoption back, a clear pattern emerged: affluent customers—those who sent and received checks most frequently—were the least likely to use MRDC. Customers who regularly deposited checks above the dollar threshold wouldn't even attempt it, let alone make it a habit. This created a genuine strategic dilemma. The conservative eligibility cutoffs reduced fraud exposure, but they also pushed away the bank’s most valuable customers. The core question became similar to a classic control limits problem in statistics: How much were the risk thresholds actually suppressing MRDC adoption and usage? And under what conditions would relaxing them make sense—where the gains from broader usage would outweigh the incremental fraud losses? Simulation as the solution to identifying business impact The path forward was to build a detailed simulation model to quantify the impact of changing the MRDC risk rules. We benchmarked competitor policies and found a clear pattern: Banks with less restrictive limits enjoyed noticeably higher MRDC adoption rates. Our simulation captured the full range of benefits from increased mobile deposit usage—lower item-processing costs, stronger customer retention, and higher deposit balances across representative customer cohorts. The objective was to find the threshold where expected fraud losses were offset by those compounding benefits. The results were compelling. Field trials confirmed that loosening the eligibility restrictions boosted customer usage without any meaningful increase in fraud losses. That confidence in our simulation’s predictive power then informed a targeted direct mail campaign to drive further adoption. How Teradata can help Teradata offers a comprehensive library of econometric functions that run directly in-database—including model training and forecasting. That makes it well-suited for developing the kind of propensity models and scenario analyses described here.

title: Firefly’s SciTec Awarded $94 Million U.S. Space Force Contract to Advance Ground-Based Radar Digitization Program

SciTec’s industry-leading software and big data processing capabilities are proven in operations for missile warning and defense; intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance; space domain awareness; remote sensing and analysis; and autonomous command and control.
